title: Filter the file browser by Intent and by changes

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-420#filter-review-files

**Verdict: Caught.** Three maintained assertions failed on the wrong behavior, which was observed separately on the path each one exercises.

Invocation start: 2026-11-26T10:02:26+08:00 (1795658546000 Unix epoch ms, host clock). The end time is appended below.

## Target
- Story and revision: .planning/seeds/SEED-420-unified-intent-review.md `#filter-review-files`, plan .planning/slice-plans/838-filter-review-files/PLAN.md, revision c94f1dc8ee28d10a01bf51326a8aa59ec5b892f1.
- Promise: "A filter removes paths from the browser and leaves the open reading and Story Home in place." Key examples: an open production file stays open when Intent only hides it, and an open untouched file stays open, without the not-in-revision notice, when Changes only hides it.
- Scratch checkout: a detached worktree of the selected revision at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/015d38ff/tmp/ic-scratch, set up with `npm ci` on Node 24.21.0. It was clean before the probe (0 porcelain lines) and has been removed.

## Fault (one edit; fixtures and assertions unchanged)
I used the caller's first suggested fault: the product clears the selection when a filter hides it. In `dashboard/src/IntentBrowser.tsx`, I replaced `const selection = storyFileSelection(storyTree.overlay, keptSelection);` with a version that turns a file selection into `{ path: "" }` (no selection) when the path is in `storyTree.overlay.files` but missing from the filtered `storyTree.shown.files`. I did not run the second suggested fault, where the filtered inventory feeds the missing check. The skill allows one fault per probe.

## Checks and commands
- Frontend: `caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard:frontend -- dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-story-changes-only.spec.ts dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-story-intent-only.spec.ts` (10 tests).
- E2E: `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES OPEN_DOUGH_E2E_PROOF_RECORD=<tmp json> caffeinate -s -i npm run test:e2e -- review/story-card-review-arrival-race.spec.ts` (3 tests).
- Command change: I ran the whole e2e spec file instead of filtering with `-g`. A `-g` run selected nothing, and the quiet reporter prints nothing when a run passes. The proof record confirms which tests ran (selectedCount 3, including the target at line 140).

## Observations
- **Baseline:** frontend 10/10 passed; e2e 3/3 passed, confirmed by the proof record.
- **Under the fault, frontend 2 failed, 8 passed:**
  - `intent-story-changes-only.spec.ts:94` "an open untouched file stays open, not called missing, when Changes only hides it".
    - Reach: the steps before the assertion ran. The test clicked kept.spec.ts, turned Changes only on, and confirmed the row was gone at line 102.
    - Caught at line 104: `readingText` toContain keptPath. The reading text was `''`.
    - Line 103 (`readingShown`) still passed because the empty reading pane stays visible. That poll alone would not catch this fault.
  - `intent-story-intent-only.spec.ts:52` "an open production file stays open, not called missing, when Intent only hides it".
    - Reach: the row was hidden at line 59.
    - Caught at line 60: `diffName` expected 'Modified dashboard/src/App.tsx' and got `''`. The open diff closed.
- **Under the fault, e2e: "choosing a file while the card's comparison is reading keeps that file" failed:**
  - The in-hold `files.expectSelected("tests/kept.spec.ts")` at line 156 passed. While the comparison is still being read, Changes only is not yet applied, so the row is still listed.
  - After the comparison arrived, `expect(purposeRegion(intent)).toContainText('test("kept source"')` at line 160 failed.
  - The Purpose region first showed "Reading tests/kept.spec.ts…". It then switched to "Added tests/changed.spec.ts … +test(\"changed source\"…)". Once the selection was cleared, the first-changed-file choice opened a different file.
  - The other 2 tests in the file passed.
- **Independent witness:** the observed values show the reading going wrong on the intended path: an empty reading text, an empty diff heading, and the e2e reading swapped to another file. The failures were not unrelated errors.
- **Restoration:** I restored the file with `git checkout`. Porcelain was back to 0 lines and HEAD was still c94f1dc8e. The same commands then passed: frontend 10/10 and e2e 3/3 (proof record phase completed). After that I removed the scratch worktree.

## Next proof action
None is needed for this fault on these paths. The e2e line 160 assertion is the one that catches it after the comparison arrives, so the rewritten arrival-race test still guards the promise. Optional: `readingShown` (changes-only line 103) does not tell an empty pane from an open reading; the readingText assertion that follows covers this. A second probe could try the other suggested fault (the filtered inventory feeding the missing check). Here the `not.toContain("is not in revision")` assertions were reached but never had to catch anything.

## Prior dispositions
This matches the execution's rewrite of the arrival-race test: the post-arrival Purpose-content assertion still catches the fault. The probe does not call for a new repair.

## Cost
- **Test runtime.** Measured, from runner-reported durations on one local machine (load average about 6–10):
  - Frontend Vitest "Duration": baseline 8.99 s, fault 9.34 s, restored 8.87 s.
  - E2E: wall time about 7.8 s baseline and 9.8 s faulted. Per-test proof-record durations for the target test were 2572 ms baseline, 6787 ms faulted and 2603 ms restored; the restored run's wall time was not separately captured.
  - Two baseline e2e runs (no `-g` match, then without a proof record) each took about 8 s of wall time.
  - Total test time is about 65 s (estimated, from the sums above).
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: this was an unattended agent run with no human interaction measured.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable as a separately supported measure. The agent made about 25 tool calls (estimated count from this session).


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 190988 ms (measured), from 1795658546000 to 1795658736988 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.


## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision c94f1dc8ee28d10a01bf51326a8aa59ec5b892f1; verdict Caught; no follow-up.
